pamphlet_excerpts: Whistle Commands Range: The whistle commands used on a range, and their relatedverbal commands, are as follows.
Blasts Whistle Shootingline: Two blasts on a whistle, ”Step to the shootingline.” You may step to the shooting line and pick upyour bow.
Blast Whistle Commence: One blast on a whistle, ”Commence shooting.” You may pick up an arrow and shoot this end.
Whenyou Done Bow: Whenyou are done, put your bow in a bow stand and stepto the waiting line. 3.
step_by_step_procedure: Blasts Whistle Retrieve: Three blasts on a whistle, ”Retrieve your arrows.” You may go downrange and retrieve your arrows.
Follow Rules Retrieving: Follow the three rules for retrieving arrows (above). 4.
Blasts Whistle STOP: Four or more blasts on a whistle, ”STOP!” or “Cease fire!” Do not shoot.
However Way Transportan: However, the best way to transportan arrow is safely in its quiver. • Be sure the area around and beyond your target is clearbefore you shoot.

quiz_item.scenario_prompt: While shooting on the archery range, an arrow slips off your bow rest and lands on the ground 4 feet in front of the shooting line while other archers are still at full draw. What must you do?
options: Lean forward across the shooting line and grab the arrow quickly before anyone notices.
Leave the arrow on the ground, never reach or step across the shooting line while the range is hot, and wait for the Range Officer's three-whistle 'Retrieve Arrows' command.
Signal your buddy in the next lane to kick the arrow back behind the waiting line.
quiz_item.correct_answer: Option B — Leave the dropped arrow untouched in front of the shooting line until the Range Officer blows three whistles to retrieve arrows.
quiz_item.explanation: Stepping or reaching across an active shooting line puts you directly in the path of adjacent bows; any arrow forward of the line is retrieved only after all bows are racked on the 3-whistle signal.

pamphlet_excerpts: Tell Arrows Apart: You also can tell arrows apart by their fletchings. • Target arrows use small fletchings.
Feathersfrom Inches Long: These can be feathersfrom 2 to 3 inches long or plastic vanes about 11/2 to 2 inches long.
Fletchings Blunt-tipped: These fletchings are most often used on blunt-tipped arrows.
They Slow Arrow: They slow the arrow’s flight and make it drop quickly. • Hunting arrows use longer fletchings, usually 4 to 5 incheslong.
step_by_step_procedure: Fletchings Strong Spiral: The fletchings usually have a strong spiral that causesthe arrow to rotate, which improves its flight when the pointis a broadhead.
Modern Arrow Shafts: Modern arrow shafts are made from four principal materials: wood, aluminum, fiberglass, or carbon fiber.
Beginning Archersusually: Beginning archersusually use arrows with wood shafts.
Wood Least Expensive: Wood is the least expensive shaft material and is popular with many archers.

requirements.lead_text: Working under the supervision of a certified USA Archery Level 1 Instructor or a certified long-term camp staff member (i.e., a National Camping School [NCS] Range Activities Director; or a Rangemaster over age 18 who is trained by an NCS Range Activities Director or by a USA Archery Level 1 Instructor), do ONE of the following options: Note: When using a Genesis bow, apply the requirements in Option A.
requirements.req_text: Working under the supervision of a certified USA Archery Level 1 Instructor or a certified long-term camp staff member (i.e., a National Camping School [NCS] Range Activities Director; or a Rangemaster over age 18 who is trained by an NCS Range Activities Director or by a USA Archery Level 1 Instructor), do ONE of the following options: Note: When using a Genesis bow, apply the requirements in Option A. (a) Option A—Recurve Bow or Longbow. Do ALL of the following: (1) Name and point to the parts of the recurve or longbow you are shooting. (2) Explain how to properly care for and store recurve bows and longbows. (3) Demonstrate and explain USA Archery's 11 Steps of Shooting for the bow you are shooting. (4) Demonstrate the proper way to string a recurve bow or longbow. (5) Using a bow square, locate and mark with dental floss, crimp-on, or other method, the nocking point on the bowstring of the bow you are using. (6) Do ONE of the following: (a) Using a recurve bow or longbow and arrows with a finger release, shoot a single round of ONE of the following: (1) An NFAA field round of 14 targets and make a score of 60 points (2) A Scouting America field round of 14 targets and make a score of 80 points (3) A World Archery/USA Archery indoor round and make a score of 80 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (4) An NFAA indoor round and make a score of 50 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (b) Shooting 30 arrows in five-arrow ends at an 80-centimeter (32-inch) five-color target at 10 yards and using the 10 scoring regions, make a score of 150 points. (b) Option B—Compound Bow. Do ALL of the following: (1) Name and point to the parts of the compound bow you are shooting. (2) Explain how to properly care for and store compound bows. (3) Demonstrate and explain USA Archery's 11 Steps of Shooting for the bow you are shooting. (4) Explain why it is necessary to have the string or cable on a compound bow replaced at an archery shop. (5) Locate and mark with dental floss, crimp-on, or other method, the nocking point on the bowstring of the bow you are using. (6) Do ONE of the following: (a) Using a compound bow and arrows with a finger release, shoot a single round of ONE of the following: (1) An NFAA field round of 14 targets and make a score of 70 points (2) A Scouting America field round of 14 targets and make a score of 90 points (3) A World Archery/USA Archery indoor round and make a score of 90 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (4) An NFAA indoor round and make a score of 60 points (Indoor rounds may be shot outdoors if this is more convenient.) (b) Shooting at an 80-centimeter (32-inch) five-color target using the 10 scoring regions, make a minimum score of 160 points. Accomplish this in the following manner: Shoot 15 arrows in five-arrow ends, at a distance of 10 yards AND Shoot 15 arrows in five-arrow ends, at a distance of 15 yards.
